instruction: Enable the 'Send a Do Not Track request' option in Chrome's privacy and security settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome and tried to navigate to google.com/preferences to change search results per page. Hit SSL certificate errors (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID) due to proxy. Spent 50 turns trying curl, terminal debugging, and various URL attempts. Never declared the task as infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome from desktop, type URLs in address bar, use keyboard shortcuts (Enter, F5), open and use terminal, interact with Chrome UI elements (buttons, address bar)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed on two fronts: (1) SSL cert errors prevented accessing google.com through the proxy, (2) never recognized the task was infeasible. Model exhausted all 50 turns without declaring [INFEASIBLE].
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a Chrome local privacy settings task (Do Not Track toggle via chrome://settings/privacy) that doesn't require internet access and is a single toggle action within model's demonstrated capabilities.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome privacy settings and enabling the Do Not Track option. Evaluator uses existing enable_do_not_track getter to read Chrome preferences and custom check_do_not_track metric to verify the value is True. [Fixed: added type coercion in metric to handle getter returning string 'true'/'false' instead of Python bool]
fix_history: Fix 1: Added type coercion in check_do_not_track metric to convert string result ('true'/'false') to Python bool before comparing with expected_enabled boolean

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_enable_do_not_track correctly reads the 'enable_do_not_track' key from Chrome's Preferences JSON file and returns 'true'/'false' strings, which is the right state for this task.

Custom metric correctly handles the string-to-bool type coercion (result.lower() == 'true') before comparing with the boolean expected_enabled value, resolving the previously identified type mismatch.
Expected parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the metric receives {'expected_enabled': true} directly and accesses it via expected.get('expected_enabled', True).
Full instruction coverage: the single requirement (enable Do Not Track) is completely verified by the evaluator.
validation.fix_description: Added type coercion in metric to handle string/bool mismatch from getter
